newsitem.title: JAPAN: Survey shows Japan kids taller, but less healthy.
newsitem.headline: Survey shows Japan kids taller, but less healthy.

text.p: Japanese schoolchildren are taller than their counterparts 30 years ago, but have poorer eyesight and are sicker because of excessive videogame playing and overstudying, a government survey showed on Friday.
Japanese high school students are on average four centimetres (1.5 inches) taller than their counterparts 30 years ago, according to the Education Ministry's 1996 School Children's Health Survey.
But more schoolchildren now suffer more from asthma, obesity, dental problems and short-sightedness than in previous years.

"Video games are undoubtedly one of the causes of the deteriorating eyesight of schoolchildren... Another cause is excessive studying for exams," said the ministry's Kazunari Asanuma, who organised the survey.
He said that short-sightedness among schoolchildren is at its highest level ever.

Many students prepare for so-called "exam hell" by attending special night schools, after their regular classes, in order to study for exams which they must pass to gain entrance to exclusive high schools and universities.
Asanuma said improvements in diet were behind today's taller kids. "In particular, since the war (World War Two), Japanese have begun to eat a lot more meat," he said.

Asanuma said the number of asthma-afflicted schoolchildren had almost tripled from 0.3 percent of all students 30 years ago to 0.8 percent this year, but that obesity among high school students at 1.4 percent compared to 1.0 percent seven years ago, was levelling off.
